section_summary.extract_value: This section discusses the implications of the present study's findings, suggesting that the relationship between learning and performance orientations and learning outcomes is more complex than previously thought, especially when cognitive ability is considered. It highlights that learning orientation was adaptive for high-ability individuals but not low-ability, and performance orientation effects depended on both ability and outcome. The section also proposes future research directions, including investigating the robustness of these interactions, task complexity as a boundary condition, and mediating process variables.
